article.headline: Republicans present revised CLARITY Act as final offer ahead of Senate vote
article.dek: Senate Republicans unveil a 635‑page amendment to the CLARITY Act, featuring Trump‑backed ethics rules and extensive changes to digital‑asset regulations, just before a procedural vote.
article.article_body:
On Sunday, Senate Republicans issued a revised version of the CLARITY Act, framing it as a final offer to Democrats before a procedural vote scheduled for Tuesday at 2:15 p.m. ET. The 635‑page proposal, introduced by the Senate Banking Digital Assets Subcommittee Chair Cynthia Lummis together with subcommittee chairmen John Boozman and Tim Scott, expands the bill’s scope to include new provisions for the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act and stablecoin yield regulations. Lummis emphasized that the revisions reflect a year of bipartisan negotiations and incorporate 126 changes requested by Democrats.

The most prominent addition is a set of ethics provisions that Lummis said were voluntarily agreed to by President Donald Trump. “After a year of intense daily bipartisan negotiations, this bill is ready,” Lummis told reporters. She added, “President Trump voluntarily agreed to unprecedented ethics restrictions, holding every federally elected official, judge, and their spouses to some of the toughest ethics restrictions in US history.” These rules would empower state attorneys general to enforce bans on federal officials who issue, sponsor, or hold significant financial interests in digital assets, and on exchanges that list assets violating those bans. Affected individuals would be required either to divest the holdings or place them in a qualified blind trust.

Violations of the new ethics rules would trigger civil penalties of $500,000 or 20 % of the transaction value, whichever is greater. The penalties would become effective 360 days after the bill’s enactment, or earlier if implementing regulations are finalized. A Republican aide described the document as the party’s “final offer” on the legislation, underscoring the urgency as the Senate prepares for the upcoming procedural vote.

While the revised CLARITY Act seeks to tighten oversight of government officials’ involvement with digital assets, it also amends the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act, aiming to clarify the regulatory framework for blockchain‑related activities. The combined changes signal a concerted effort by Senate Republicans to shape the nation’s digital‑asset policy before the bill advances to the Senate floor.

Stakeholders across the crypto industry will be watching the outcome of Tuesday’s vote closely, as the final form of the CLARITY Act could set precedent‑defining standards for ethics, stablecoin regulation, and broader blockchain oversight in the United States.
